narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To illustrate that younger generations are the primary drivers of Black migration to the South, supporting the narrator's explanation about increased educational opportunities for newer generations.

units.meaning: The 18-29 age group has the highest value in the chart, at 24%.

basis.note: Table unit is %; this is the maximum value among the five age groups.

accepted_routes: The 18-29 age group has the largest value, 24%.
18-29 is the top age bracket at 24%.
The highest value is the 18-29 group at 24%.
Adults 18-29 lead with 24%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 18-29 mark must be visibly the highest and labeled or annotated with 24%.
units.temporal_anchor: I attribute some of it to younger generations
units.reviewer_question: Should the video explicitly identify 18-29 as the largest group and state 24%, or is the tallest mark enough?

units.meaning: The 5-17 and 30-44 age groups are tied for the second-highest value at 17% each.

basis.note: Table unit is %; equal to the 5-17 value.

accepted_routes: The 5-17 and 30-44 groups are tied at 17%.
Both 5-17 and 30-44 have 17%, behind only 18-29.
The second-highest value is shared by 5-17 and 30-44, each at 17%.
Two age groups, 5-17 and 30-44, both show 17%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 5-17 and 30-44 marks must be visibly equal in height and labeled 17% each, or otherwise shown as tied.
units.reviewer_question: Is the tie between 5-17 and 30-44 at 17% required detail, or optional?

units.meaning: The 45-59 age group has the lowest value at 9%, below the 60+ group at 13%.

basis.note: Table unit is %; this is the minimum value among the five age groups.

accepted_routes: The 45-59 group is the lowest at 9%.
45-59 has the smallest value, 9%.
The 45-59 bracket trails with 9%, below 60+ at 13%.
The lowest mark is 45-59 at 9%, while 60+ is higher at 13%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 45-59 mark must be visibly the lowest and labeled 9%, with the 60+ mark labeled 13% and shown higher.
units.reviewer_question: Does the video need to show 45-59 as the lowest at 9%, or is that dispensable?

units.meaning: The full ranking of age groups by value is 18-29 (24%) > 5-17 = 30-44 (17% each) > 60+ (13%) > 45-59 (9%).
accepted_routes: Order from highest to lowest: 18-29 (24%), then 5-17 and 30-44 (17% each), then 60+ (13%), then 45-59 (9%).
18-29 leads; 5-17 and 30-44 tie for second; 60+ is fourth; 45-59 is last.
From highest to lowest, the values are 24%, 17%, 17%, 13%, and 9%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The relative heights of all five age-group marks must match the ranking, or an on-screen ordered list or labels must show it.
units.temporal_anchor: I attribute some of it to younger generations
units.reviewer_question: Should the full age-group ranking be explicitly conveyed, or is highlighting the top group sufficient?

units.meaning: The 18-29 group alone (24%) is larger than the 45-59 and 60+ groups combined (9% + 13% = 22%).
accepted_routes: The 18-29 group alone (24%) is larger than the 45-59 and 60+ groups combined (9% + 13% = 22%).
24% for 18-29 exceeds the combined 22% for the two oldest groups.
The single 18-29 bracket outweighs the 45-59 and 60+ brackets together, 24 vs 22.
45-59 plus 60+ totals 22%, which is less than the 24% for 18-29 alone.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 18-29 mark must be shown as taller than the 45-59 and 60+ marks combined, or an annotation must state 24 vs 22.
units.temporal_anchor: I attribute some of it to younger generations
units.reviewer_question: Should the video compare 18-29 against the two oldest groups combined (24 vs 22), or only show individual bars?

optional_valid: The 18-29 value is about 1.4 times the 17% values for 5-17 and 30-44 (24 / 17 = 1.41).
The 18-29 value is about 1.8 times the 13% for 60+ (24 / 13 = 1.85).
The 18-29 value is about 2.7 times the 9% for 45-59 (24 / 9 = 2.67).
The three age groups under 45 (5-17 + 18-29 + 30-44 = 17 + 24 + 17 = 58) sum to 58, compared with 22 for 45+ (45-59 + 60+ = 9 + 13 = 22).
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claim that advanced education opportunities caused younger generations to migrate.
Absolute counts of Black migrants or population numbers.
Claims about age groups not present in the table.
Assuming the displayed values sum to 100% or represent the entire migration population.
Treating the relative_value column as a percentage rather than a 0-1 normalization.
Extrapolating a time trend, since the table has no time series.
notes: Values are percentages per the table's unit; derived comparisons use only sums or ratios of those values. The key trade-off is whether the full age-group ranking is required or only the 18-29 lead and its comparison to older groups.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
